prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: desktop web app layout decision comp, 16:10 landscape
Primary request: Create a high-fidelity north-star mockup for the Spectro unified event explorer using the “Focus Bench” structure. This is an operational interface, not a marketing page.
Reference image: carry over only Spectro’s existing chrome, cool daylight palette, Avenir-like humanist typography, compact monospaced telemetry, hairline borders, restrained ultraviolet/cyan signal accents, white instrument surfaces, and gently rounded 12–16px containers. Do not carry over the foundation page’s hero copy, signal-path diagram, or split landing-page composition.
Structure: a slim left navigation rail; across the top of the workspace a project/environment/time command bar; directly below it a wide compact event-volume time ruler with tick marks and a sparse violet/cyan signal trace; below, a dense chronological event ledger taking about 60% width and a persistent context detail bench taking about 40%. The selected event aligns across ledger and inspector with one precise ultraviolet marker. The detail bench shows Event, Context, and Raw tabs, contextual project/environment/session/page/release values, and structured payload rows. Filters are compact, familiar controls, not decorative tiles.
Content: clearly label all data as illustrative. Use realistic Spectro event names such as runtime_error, web_vital_lcp, fetch_request, element_click, checkout_completed. Show project prj_checkout, environment production, a Last 30 minutes range, and one selected runtime_error with session/page/release context.
Style: quiet precision instrument in cool daylight, 90% neutral and 10% signal; flat by default; one focused surface may have a diffuse lift.
Constraints: readable dense UI, familiar controls, semantic hierarchy, no gradients as decoration, no black dashboard, no KPI card grid, no floating glass panels, no sidebar full of colorful icons, no fabricated customers or metrics, no watermark. Avoid tiny illegible text; prioritize clear spatial hierarchy over exact copy.
